thread:
marta: Thinking about automatic variant fallback when the primary model is saturated — should fallbacks be weighted by customer tier and region or left global? :thinking:
ajay: We have a global fallback today and it's causing complaints from premium customers who get a lower-quality variant during spikes.
lee: I'd prefer per-customer policy: fallback_enabled, allowed_variants list, and a max_fallback_rate. That way we can protect SLAs for enterprise.
priya: For telemetry we need fallback_count, fallback_rate_by_tier, fallback_latency_delta, and a quality_regression signal (eval hooks). Tag metrics by region and route.
ben: Console UX idea: show a "Fallback impact" panel in the rollout / model page with a heatmap by region and tier + quick toggle "block fallback for this customer". Also per-route override.
marta: Important: we must distinguish capacity-driven saturation (queue/alloc) vs transient latency blips. Use capacity_signal (gpu_util, queue_depth) + sustained p95 increase before auto-fallback.
ajay: API thought — add optional headers so callers can opt out: `X-Allow-Variant-Fallback: true|false` and `X-Fallback-Policy: weighted|priority|round_robin`. Also, servers should return `X-Selected-Model-Variant` in response for telemetry.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary fallback-policy-service -> staging (10%) at 2024-11-09T15:30:00Z :rocket:
priya: Add a circuit breaker: if fallback paths increase error rate or reduce quality (based on eval hooks) beyond threshold (e.g., error_rate + quality_drop > 2% over 5m) then auto-revert and page SRE. We also need a metric for cost_delta per-token when falling back (some variants cheaper).
lee: Config prototype (example we discussed):
```json
{"policy_name": "tiered_weighted_fallback_v1", "priority": ["tier","region","route"], "defaults": {"free": {"allowed": true, "max_rate": 0.5}, "standard": {"allowed": true, "max_rate": 0.1}, "enterprise": {"allowed": false, "max_rate": 0.0}}, "variants": [{"model":"m-1.1-q4","weight":0.7},{"model":"m-1.0-q8","weight":0.3}], "signals": {"capacity_threshold": 0.85, "sustained_ms": 300000}}
```
ben: For product reporting, include a fallback_drift chart (expected quality vs actual) and top impacted customers list. PMs will want an exportable CSV for weekly reviews.
marta: Plan: prototype in staging with the new headers + policy config, wire telemetry, add console mockups, and then canary 10% customers. @ajay can you own the API/header PR? @priya own metrics and alerts? @lee own console changes?
ajay: I can take the API work. Quick q — default policy for free/dev users? allow fallback aggressively by default?
priya: Recommend defaults: free/dev => allow fallback (max_rate 50%), standard => soft fallback (10%), enterprise => blocked unless explicitly enabled. We can make these defaults configurable per-commit.
marta: Cool. I'll draft an RFC and share mocks. RFC link: https://r.rwd/internal/rfcs/variant-fallback-1768509876
ajay: I'll open the API PR after the RFC.
priya: I'll add metrics names to the RFC (fallback.count, fallback.rate, fallback.latency_delta, fallback.quality_regression, fallback.cost_delta).
ben: Adding console mock request to UX board.
marta: Thanks all — next sync Thurs to review staging metrics. :thumbsup:
